label: Content-fixed favouring laws, from the definitions
meaning: Law 1: the actual history h and a history k with another outcome are both in the realized range; selection at h gives favouring of out h over out k, at k favouring of out k over out h, by the same content, contradicting asymmetry. Law 2 checks the re-description directly; a contingent outcome makes its content differ between two histories. Law 3: one cell relates every two histories. Law 4: selection would favour the actual outcome over the tied rival, which good-boundedness turns into a G-ranking. Law 5: the bettering outcome is distinct by asymmetry, and selection over it gives the reverse G-ranking.
